T178. Stiff-Person Syndrome and Ophthalmoplegia
Associated with Thymoma
Eugene C. Lai, I. Linfante, and A. G. Lee; Houston, TX
We report the clinical presentation, antibody production,
and symptom improvement after treatment of a unique case
of paraneoplastic syndrome associated with thymoma. We
followed the clinical course of a previously healthy 44-year-
old Caucasian woman for 6 months. She presented with sub-

acute onset of double vision and leg spasm for 4 weeks until
she was unable to move her eyes or walk. Ophthalmological
examination revealed complete ophthalmoplegia but normal
visual acuity and optic disc. Neurological examination dem-
onstrated severe spasticity and hyperreflexia in her legs, spar-
ing her arms. She could not walk because of pain and stiff-
ness. The rest of her examination was unremarkable. Her
workup revealed a mediastinal mass and a markedly elevated
anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase (anti-GAD) antibody titer.
Pathological diagnosis of the excised mass was mixed-type
thymoma with local extension into the mediastinal adipose
tissue and adherence to the pericardium. Therefore, she also
underwent radiation therapy. Extensive workup did not
identify any other cause of her problem. She was treated with
intravenous methylprednisolone, but her symptoms and anti-
GAD titer persisted. She then received intrathecal baclofen
therapy and plasmapheresis followed by gammaglobulin
treatment. Her ophthalmoplegia and stiffness improved no-
tably as documented by video. She was able to walk with
minimal assistance. Repeat studies did not reveal evidence of
myasthenia gravis. To our knowledge, this is the first docu-
mented case of stiff-person syndrome and ophthalmoplegia
associated with thymoma.
